discussion:
The use of Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) can introduce additional security risks to networks if not managed appropriately. As such, IPv6 capable network security appliances should be used on IPv6 and dual-stack networks to ensure security coverage equivalent to that provided for Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4) networks while assisting in ensuring that IPv6 cannot be exploited by malicious actors.

To aid in the transition from IPv4 to IPv6, numerous tunnelling protocols have been developed to enable interoperability between IPv4 and IPv6. Disabling IPv6 tunnelling protocols on networks that do not require such functionality will prevent malicious actors from bypassing traditional network defences by encapsulating IPv6 data inside IPv4 packets.

Stateless Address Autoconfiguration is a method of stateless Internet Protocol (IP) address configuration in IPv6 networks. It reduces the ability of an organisation to maintain effective logs of IP address assignments on networks. For this reason, stateless IP addressing should be avoided.
title: IPv6 capable network security appliances are used on IPv6 and dual-stack networks.
